newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Nov 20.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English-born journalist and broadcaster ALISTAIR COOKE, who was best-known for his radio programme 'Letter from America', was born in 1908.
Australian jazz musician and bandleader RAY PRICE was born in 1921. He played bass, guitar and banjo.
South African novelist NADINE GORDIMER, who was an anti-apartheid campaigner and winner of the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1991, was born in 1923.

American Senator ROBERT KENNEDY was born in 1925. He was presidential campaign manager for his brother JOHN F. KENNEDY in 1960 and as attorney-general 1961-64 promoted the Civil Rights Act. After J.F.K's assassination and LYNDON B. JOHNSON's selection of HUBERT HUMPHREY as his vice-presidential nomination ROBERT resigned and was elected senator for New York. In 1968 he was assassinated during a campaign stop in California.
English/Australian pop singer with the yodel FRANK IFIELD was born in 1937. His hits included "I Remember You", "Lovesick Blues" and "Please".
British drummer and singer with 'UB40' JAMES BROWN was born in 1957.
** EVENTS **
1497 : VASCO DA GAMA became the first European to round
the Cape of Good Hope and complete a voyage to the sub-continent.
1902 : Grandson of the poet LORD TENNYSON was appointed
governor-general of Australia.
1918 : The German High Seas Fleet surrendered at the
Firth of Forth in Scotland, one of the key conditions of the armistice signed on Nov 11.
1920 : The Irish Republican Army shot dead 14 British
soldiers in what became known as the country's first "Bloody Sunday".
1925 : A law was passed in Italy banning the Freemasons
and other secret societies.
1926 : Australia was declared a self-governing dominion.

At the Imperial Conference in London the oldest former colonies of the British Empire were granted equal status with Britain. In addition to Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Canada and Newfoundland had their status altered. The countries were said to now be "masters of their own destinies".
1929 : Modern artist SALVADOR DALI held his first one-man
show in Paris.
1944 : London's Picadilly Circus and the Strand were
ablaze with lights after five years of wartime blackouts.
1945 : The trial of senior Nazis officials charged with

war crimes began in Nuremberg. The 24 defendants included Luftwaffe leader HERMANN GOERING, an early proponent of the anti-semitic philosophy JULIUS STREICHER and HITLER's deputy RUDOLP HESS. Absent were HITLER, GOEBBELS and HIMMLER. They committed suicide rather than face trial.
1947 : Princess ELIZABETH, heir to the throne, married
Lieutenant PHILIP MOUNTBATTEN at Westminister Abbey. The groom was created Prince PHILIP, Duke of Edinburgh, by the King at a ceremony at Buckingham Palace before the wedding.
1967 : Polish-born American scientist, CASIMIR FUNK, who
invented the word "vitamin", died at the age of 83.
1970 : More than 150,000 people died in the typhoon and
tidal wave in East Pakistan. The tidal wave, as high as a two-storey building, struck at midnight.
1972 : A prominent Soviet nuclear scientist joined 50

other civil rights campaigners in urging the Kremlin to abolish the death penalty and to free all politicial prisoners. ANDREI SAKHAROV, who was involved in the development of the Russian H-bomb was also the founder of the Moscow Human Rights committee in 1970. He also actively campaigned for a partial ban on nuclear testing.
1979 : Surveyor of the Queen's Pictures Sir ANTHONY BLUNT
was stripped of his knighthood after admitting to spying for Russia in collusion with BURGESS, MACLEAN and PHILBY.
1981 : A second inquest was ordered into the death of

AZARIA CHAMBERLAIN after Northern Territory police presented new evidence. Mr Justice TOOHEY said, if accepted, the new evidence was likely to prove that the dingo did not take the baby. Four days later police at Alice Springs began a new search for the baby's body.
1986 : British police searched Saddleworth Moor for two
missing children, feared killed, after MYRA HINDLEY broke her silence.
1994 : The United Nations Security Council voted to
authorise NATO air strikes on Bosnian-Serb positions, as the conflict in northern Bosnia escalated.
1995 : Parties at the Bosnia peace tallks in Dayton,
Ohio, agreed to an accord ending the bloody Balkan conflict.
1995 : Acting Prime Minister SHIMON PERES formed a new
Israeli government following the assassination of YITZHAK RABIN.
